This module cites no new regulation, guidance, or standard — it's a synthesis exercise,
combining evidence this course already built in depth, the same handling
`designing-an-internal-audit-program`'s own resources page gave its own synthesis-only
module. Nothing below is quoted in this lesson. These links point back to the primary
sources this course has already verified and cited at length, so you can go straight to the
actual text behind today's two re-referenced phrases, rather than a brand-new search for
sources this module doesn't need.

- **[Cornell LII: 21 U.S.C. § 374](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/21/374)** —
  reused from `fda-inspection-authority-and-outcomes`. The full statutory text behind
  374(a)(1)'s inspection authority and 374(b)(1)'s written-report requirement — the actual
  legal basis for everything the morning, FDA-style mock session can ask to see.

- **[AABB: Accreditation Process](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/accreditation/become-accredited/accreditation-process)**
  — reused from `the-aabb-assessment-process`. AABB's own public description of its
  two-phase process, including the "PPPs... followed as written" sentence this module's
  afternoon session is built around. Read it for the full context this module only
  re-references in one line.

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR § 606.160](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.160)**
  — reused from `data-integrity-and-records`. The full text of 606.160(e), including the
  "at least monthly" floor this module's cadence decision is measured against. This course
  never quoted (e) in full itself; read it here if you want the actual regulatory floor
  behind Lakeshore's own weekly decision, not just this module's paraphrase of it.

Four more places go further than this lesson needs to, including the video embedded above.

- **[FDA Drug Manufacturing Inspections - REdI 2020](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1-z4NCmXEV8)**
  (U.S. Food and Drug Administration, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this
  lesson. FDA's own training session on how its drug-manufacturing inspections run and how a
  firm prepares for, hosts, and responds to one. Drug CGMP, not blood-establishment or
  21 CFR 606 specific, so use it for the investigator's-eye view of the room, not for
  blood-specific requirements. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Inspection Observations](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/inspection-references/inspection-observations)**
  — FDA's own public page on inspectional observations and Form 483, the document a mock
  session's closing meeting rehearses. Read it before running a mock, so your findings log is
  shaped like what a real investigator hands over. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/data-integrity-and-compliance-drug-cgmp-questions-and-answers)**
  — the FDA data-integrity Q&A behind ALCOA's "accurate" element, the test DED-0458's fifth
  letter was run against. Drug-CGMP guidance, so read it for how FDA thinks about data
  integrity, not as a blood-specific rule. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Blood Guidances](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/biologics-guidances/blood-guidances)**
  — CBER's index of its blood-specific guidance documents. When a mock reviewer asks "where
  does FDA say that for blood establishments," start here instead of a drug or device source.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

If you want the general, non-regulatory background on how a mock inspection or mock audit
is typically run in a regulated industry, ASQ's (American Society for Quality) own public
materials on internal-audit program maturity are a reasonable starting point — the same
industry-practice tier `designing-an-internal-audit-program` already drew on, described
there in this curriculum's own words rather than quoted or cited to a specific
body-of-knowledge section number.

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about running mock inspections and inspection-readiness rooms.

- **[Mock BIMO Inspections: A Basic Guide to Readiness in 2026](https://www.thefdagroup.com/blog/mock-bimo-inspection)** (The FDA Group, consulting firm; vendor content) — explains how a mock inspection is staged and what it should test. Written for clinical-research inspections, but the mock-inspection mechanics carry over. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[FDA Inspection Plan - 3 Keys to Be Successful](https://www.mastercontrol.com/gxp-lifeline/three-keys-to-successful-fda-inspections-preparation-management-and-follow-up/)** (MasterControl, quality-software vendor; vendor content) — covers preparation, managing the inspection day, and follow-up, including how requests are tracked. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Mock FDA Inspections](https://www.lachmanconsultants.com/mock-fda-inspections/)** (Lachman Consultants, consultancy; vendor content) — a consultancy's description of what a mock inspection delivers; useful for seeing how professionals scope one. Marketing page, so read for ideas only. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
